name: Phuket
tagline: Thailand's largest island, a wide range of beach resorts, an atmospheric Sino-Portuguese old town, and the country's busiest gateway to the Andaman Sea's limestone islands.
highlight: Phuket Old Town's pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses at golden hour, their painted facades unlike any other Thai city.
shortDescription: Thailand's largest island, home to a genuine range of beach resorts, an atmospheric old town, and easy boat access to the Andaman Sea's islands.
metaDescription: A Phuket travel guide: the best beaches, Phuket Old Town, day trips, when to go and a practical four-day itinerary.
knownFor: Beaches, Phuket Old Town, island-hopping, nightlife
goodFor: Beaches, island-hopping, nightlife, a resort base

image.file: File:Phang Nga Bay, Karst islands, Thailand.jpg
image.alt: Limestone karst islands rising from the Andaman Sea near Phuket

intro: Phuket is Thailand's largest island and its best-known beach destination, a wide-ranging mix of high-rise resort strips, quieter coves and an atmospheric old town that together attract a considerably broader range of visitors than the party-island reputation alone suggests.

The island's beaches range hugely in character, from Patong's dense resorts, bars and nightlife to Kata and Karon's more relaxed family-friendly stretches and Kamala's quieter, upscale feel, giving Phuket a genuine range within a single, easily connected island.

Beyond the beaches, Phuket Old Town's pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses, built by Chinese tin-mining merchants in the 19th century, offer a different side of the island, and Phuket's size and infrastructure make it Thailand's busiest launch point for day trips to Phang Nga Bay and the Phi Phi Islands.

whyVisit.intro: Phuket's case is that its size and infrastructure offer more range — beaches, culture and island access — than any other single spot on Thailand's Andaman coast.

points.title: The beaches span every mood
points.text: From Patong's high-energy strip to Kata and Kamala's quieter, more relaxed stretches, all within a short drive of each other.

points.title: Phuket Old Town is distinct from the beach resorts
points.text: Pastel Sino-Portuguese architecture and a serious food scene, a world apart from the coastal strips.

points.title: It's Thailand's easiest launch point for island-hopping
points.text: Phang Nga Bay and the Phi Phi Islands are both straightforward day trips from Phuket's ports.

points.title: The infrastructure is the best on this coast
points.text: A wide range of hotels, restaurants and an international airport make Phuket the most convenient Andaman base.

points.title: It works for a wide range of trip styles
points.text: Suited to families, couples, nightlife-focused groups and quieter escapes, depending on which beach you choose.

attractionsIntro: Phuket's essential sights, spanning its beaches, old town and surrounding waters.

attractions.name: Phuket Old Town

image.alt: Pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses along a street in Phuket Old Town

attractions.text: Pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses built by 19th-century Chinese tin-mining merchants, one of Thailand's most distinctive architectural districts.
attractions.tip: Visit on a Sunday evening for the Lard Yai Walking Street market, when the old town's streets close to traffic.

attractions.name: Big Buddha Phuket
attractions.text: A 45-metre white marble Buddha statue crowning a hill in the island's south, offering sweeping views across Phuket and the surrounding sea.
attractions.tip: Visit in the late afternoon for the clearest views and cooler temperatures for the walk up to the statue's base.

attractions.name: Wat Chalong
attractions.text: Phuket's most important Buddhist temple, its ornate multi-tiered chedi holding relics of the Buddha, worth a stop for the island's most significant religious site.
attractions.tip: Dress modestly, as with any Thai temple — shoulders and knees covered.

attractions.name: Phang Nga Bay

image.file: File:Phang Nga Bay, Karst islands, Thailand.jpg
image.alt: Limestone karst islands rising from the Andaman Sea near Phuket

attractions.text: A dramatic seascape of limestone karst islands rising sheer from the water, including the famous James Bond Island, best explored by longtail boat or sea kayak.
attractions.tip: A sea kayak tour into the bay's hidden lagoons (hongs) offers a more intimate experience than a large tour boat.

attractions.name: The Phi Phi Islands
attractions.text: A stunning day-trip destination of turquoise water and dramatic cliffs, including Maya Bay, made famous by film and now managed with visitor limits to protect the reef.
attractions.tip: Book an early-departure boat tour to reach Maya Bay before the midday crowds, when visitor numbers are capped and controlled.

attractions.name: Kata and Karon beaches
attractions.text: Two of Phuket's most consistently recommended beaches, offering a good balance of scenery, facilities and a calmer atmosphere than Patong.
attractions.tip: Kata's smaller cove and Karon's longer stretch both work well for swimming outside the rainy-season monsoon months.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the beaches, Phuket rewards its old town, food scene and easy access to the water.

thingsToDo.title: Take a longtail boat to a nearby island
thingsToDo.text: Coral Island and Racha Island both offer excellent snorkelling and clear water within a short boat ride of Phuket's beaches.
thingsToDo.tip: A half-day trip to Coral Island is a good option if you don't have time for a full Phi Phi Islands day.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Phuket Old Town's food scene
thingsToDo.text: A strong mix of Peranakan (Chinese-Malay) cuisine, street food and coffee shops set within the old town's historic shophouses.
thingsToDo.tip: Try Hokkien mee and moo hong, two distinctive Phuket-Peranakan dishes rarely found elsewhere in Thailand.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the sunset from Promthep Cape
thingsToDo.text: Phuket's southernmost point offers a spectacular sunset viewpoint over the Andaman Sea, one of the island's most popular evening spots.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive at least 30 minutes ahead of sunset — the viewpoint's car park fills up quickly on clear evenings.

thingsToDo.title: Experience Patong's nightlife
thingsToDo.text: Bangla Road's bars, clubs and street performances offer a high-energy nightlife scene, Phuket's best-known after dark.
thingsToDo.tip: Patong's nightlife is distinct from the island's quieter beach towns — expect a considerably louder, livelier atmosphere.

thingsToDo.title: Visit an elephant sanctuary
thingsToDo.text: Several reputable ethical elephant sanctuaries near Phuket offer observation, feeding and bathing without riding or performances.
thingsToDo.tip: Research sanctuaries carefully, as with anywhere in Thailand — look for ones that explicitly prohibit riding.

thingsToDo.title: Go diving or snorkelling around the Similan Islands
thingsToDo.text: A multi-day boat trip further north to the Similan Islands offers some of Thailand's best diving, with visibility and marine life considerably beyond what's found close to Phuket itself.
thingsToDo.tip: The Similans are seasonal, typically open from mid-October to mid-May — book well ahead in peak season.

foodIntro: Phuket's food scene blends standard Thai cuisine with a distinct Peranakan (Chinese-Malay) heritage.

foods.name: Hokkien mee (Phuket-style)
foods.text: A distinctive Phuket dish of stir-fried yellow noodles with pork, seafood and vegetables, a Peranakan specialty found almost nowhere else in Thailand.
foods.whereToTry: Phuket Old Town's noodle shops, several with decades of history.

foods.name: Moo hong
foods.text: Slow-braised pork belly in a sweet, dark soy sauce, a genuine Phuket-Peranakan comfort dish with real depth of flavour.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants throughout Phuket Old Town.

foods.name: Fresh seafood
foods.text: Grilled fish, prawns and shellfish, excellent around Phuket's coastal towns, typically priced by weight and grilled simply.
foods.whereToTry: Seafood restaurants along Rawai and Chalong beaches, where the day's catch is often on direct display.

foods.name: O aew
foods.text: A refreshing Phuket dessert of chilled grass jelly, coconut milk and syrup, a distinctive local specialty rarely found outside the island.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls throughout Phuket Old Town, especially around the Sunday Walking Street market.

foods.name: Pad thai

image.alt: A plate of pad thai with pork

foods.text: Available across the island as elsewhere in Thailand, good from Phuket's street stalls and markets.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls throughout the old town and near the main beaches.

accommodation.intro: Phuket's beaches each offer a distinct atmosphere, from high-energy Patong to quieter southern coves.

areas.name: Patong
areas.bestFor: Nightlife and a wide range of hotels and restaurants
areas.text: The island's busiest, liveliest beach town, with the widest range of accommodation and Bangla Road's nightlife strip.

areas.name: Kata and Karon
areas.bestFor: A calmer beach atmosphere for families and couples
areas.text: Two of the island's most consistently recommended beaches, offering good facilities without Patong's intensity.

areas.name: Phuket Old Town
areas.bestFor: History, food and a break from the beach resorts
areas.text: A different base, putting the Sino-Portuguese architecture and food scene within walking distance, a short drive from the beaches.

gettingThere.intro: Phuket International Airport handles frequent domestic and international flights, making the island Thailand's most accessible beach destination.

options.text: Frequent direct flights from [[bangkok|Bangkok]] and international routes from across Asia.
options.detail: A metered taxi, ride-hailing app or pre-booked transfer covers the roughly 45-minute journey to Patong.

options.text: Regular connections link Phuket to [[krabi-railay|Krabi]] in about 3 hours by road.
options.detail: A private transfer avoids the multiple stops a shared minivan often makes along the way.

options.mode: Ferry to Koh Samui or Koh Phi Phi
options.text: Direct ferries connect Phuket to nearby islands, including a route toward [[koh-samui-koh-phangan|Koh Samui]] via Krabi.
options.detail: High-season ferry schedules are more frequent than during the rainy season — check current timetables ahead.

gettingAround.intro: Phuket is large for an island, so most visitors rely on taxis, ride-hailing apps or a rented scooter to get between beaches.

options.text: A popular way to explore the island's beaches and viewpoints independently, though traffic and road conditions require genuine caution.
options.detail: A proper helmet and an International Driving Permit are important — insurance often excludes claims without one.

options.text: Widely available, though metered taxis are less common than in Bangkok — negotiate or use an app for a fixed fare.
options.detail: Ride-hailing apps avoid the fare disputes that unmetered taxi trips can involve.

options.text: Shared pickup trucks run fixed routes between Phuket Town and the main beaches, a cheap if less flexible option.
options.detail: Services typically stop in the early evening — plan accordingly for a late return.

bestTime.headline: November–April, for the driest Andaman coast weather
bestTime.summary: Phuket's dry season offers the most reliable weather for beaches and island-hopping, while the monsoon months bring rougher seas on this side of the country.

seasons.text: The most comfortable and reliable weather for beaches, boat trips and island-hopping, alongside the year's biggest crowds.
Still dry and swimmable, hot but with thinner crowds than the December–January peak.
The Andaman coast's wetter, rougher-sea season — boat trips can be cancelled or curtailed, though rates drop noticeably.

bestTime.avoid: Late boat departures during the rainy season from May to October, when Andaman coast seas can turn rough with little warning.

itinerary.title: Four days in Phuket
itinerary.intro: The beaches and old town first, then island-hopping into the surrounding waters.

days.title: Arrive and settle in
days.morning: Arrive and transfer to your chosen beach.
days.afternoon: A first swim and relax at your resort's beach.
days.evening: Dinner and a first look at your area's evening scene.

days.title: Phuket Old Town
days.morning: Explore the Sino-Portuguese shophouses and street art.
days.afternoon: Lunch at a genuine Peranakan restaurant.

days.title: The Phi Phi Islands
days.morning: An early-departure boat tour to Maya Bay and the Phi Phi Islands.
days.afternoon: Snorkelling around the islands' clear water.
days.evening: A relaxed dinner back on Phuket.

days.title: Phang Nga Bay or a beach day
days.morning: A longtail boat or kayak tour through Phang Nga Bay's karsts.
days.afternoon: A final beach afternoon at Kata or Karon.
days.evening: A final dinner and, if timed right, Patong's nightlife.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, timing and transport that make a real difference to a Phuket trip.
tips: Choose your beach carefully — Patong, Kata and Karon offer different atmospheres, and moving later is inconvenient.
Wear a proper helmet if renting a scooter, and check your travel insurance covers it before riding.
Book Phi Phi Islands and Phang Nga Bay tours through a reputable operator, and choose an early departure to beat the crowds.
Avoid late boat departures during the rainy season from May to October, when seas can turn rough.
Research elephant sanctuaries carefully — choose ones that explicitly prohibit riding.
Book accommodation well ahead for the December–January peak, when Phuket's prices and crowds both spike.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Phuket?
faq.a: Four to five. Three covers a beach stay with one island day trip at a rushed pace; five allows both Phang Nga Bay and the Phi Phi Islands without feeling hurried.

faq.q: Which Phuket beach should I choose?
faq.a: Patong for nightlife and the widest range of hotels; Kata or Karon for a calmer, more relaxed atmosphere suited to families and couples; Kamala for a quieter, more upscale feel.

faq.q: Is Phuket or Krabi better for a first trip?
faq.a: Phuket offers considerably more infrastructure, nightlife and flight options; Krabi and Railay offer more dramatic scenery and a quieter, climbing-focused atmosphere. Many first-time visitors combine both.
Yes, generally — the main practical risks are scooter accidents among inexperienced riders and rough seas during the rainy season, both manageable with proper precautions.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: November to April offers the most reliable dry-season weather for beaches and island-hopping. May to October brings the Andaman coast's rainy season, with rougher seas and cancelled boat trips more common.
